title: Dynamics of two bosons with density-assisted tunnelling in a one-dimensional tilted lattice
authors: Muhammad S. Hasan, Vikash Mittal, Tomasz Sowiński
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of two bosons in a tilted one-dimensional optical lattice with both standard and density-assisted tunnelling. The relative sign of the two tunnelling processes strongly affects the Bloch dynamics, leading to distinct reinforcing and competing regimes. We examine how the tunnelling processes generate correlations and find that, in the absence of onsite interactions, the early-time entanglement growth follows the same scaling with the density-assisted tunnelling amplitude. Finite onsite interaction changes this picture by breaking the symmetry between the reinforcing and competing regimes and enhancing the correlation differently in two regimes. This shows how the interplay between the two tunnelling mechanisms can change dyanmics and entanglement in a controlled few-body setting. Particularly, at equal tunnelling amplitudes, the doublon and singlon sectors decouple completely for arbitrary onsite interaction, lattice tilting, and initial state.
summary: This theoretical study examines how two bosons behave in a tilted optical lattice when two types of tunnelling—standard and density-assisted—compete or reinforce each other. By controlling the relative strength of these tunnelling terms, the authors map out distinct dynamical regimes, showing that the interplay can lead to unique phenomena like the complete decoupling of particle sectors. This is highly relevant for understanding correlated quantum transport in cold atom setups.
main_problem: The study investigates the quantum dynamics and entanglement of two bosons moving in a one-dimensional tilted optical lattice, focusing on the interplay between standard and density-assisted tunnelling.
main_result: The interplay between the two tunnelling mechanisms can drastically alter dynamics and entanglement, notably leading to a complete decoupling of the doublon and singlon sectors under specific conditions.
method: The dynamics are calculated by time-evolving the state in the Fock basis, analyzing observables like entanglement entropy and density profiles.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by two spinless bosons in a 1D optical lattice described by an extended Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian that includes standard hopping (J), linear tilt (F), onsite interaction (U), and density-assisted tunnelling (T).
key_observables: Total density, doublon density, singlon density, Hellinger distance (H(t)), and Von Neumann Entropy (S(t)).
important_parameters: The relative strength and sign of the two tunnelling processes, controlled by a parameter $\lambda$, and the onsite interaction $U$.
main_assumptions: The analysis involves splitting the system into doublon and singlon subspaces, and some calculations are truncated to low orders in time ($O(t^3)$).
figures_summary: The notes describe how Hellinger distance and entropy evolve differently for positive versus negative $\lambda$, and how density profiles exhibit static backgrounds or oscillations depending on the relative tunnelling strengths.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Hamiltonian by varying the relative tunnelling strengths ($\lambda$), examining the resulting density dynamics, entanglement growth (entropy), and the special decoupling case when $J=T$.
why_interesting: This work provides a controlled, few-body setting to study how different types of correlated hopping terms (density-assisted tunnelling) modify fundamental quantum transport phenomena like Bloch oscillations and entanglement generation in ultracold atomic systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Time-evolved density distributions ntot i (t) of two non- interacting bosons (U = 0) for standard hopping only λ = 0, (left column) and density-assisted tunnelling only λ = 1 (right column). The top row shows both bosons initially localised at the centre of the lattice with σ2 = 0. The middle row shows Gaussian wave packet with width σ2 = 25. In the bottom row, the time evolved density mi(t) of the superposition of states where the bosons separated by one empty site is shown. The time evolution is performed over t = [0, 2τ].

FIG. 2. Time-evolved density distributions for non-interacting bosons, (U = 0) prepared initially in a Gaussian state (3) with σ2 = 25. Top row shows total density ntot i . Singlon density n(1) i and doublon density n(2) i are shown in middle and bottom rows, respectively. At λ = 0, all three densities exhibit regular Bloch oscillations with period τ = 2π/F. At λ = +1/2, the doublon density is completely frozen due to destructive interference between J and T, while singlons remain oscillatory. The reinforcing regime λ < 0 produces enhanced oscillation amplitudes, whereas the competitive regime λ > 0 leads to reduced amplitudes and the emergence of a non-oscillating background. FIG. 3. Hellinger distance H (t) as a function of time and different λ. For λ = 0, H (t) = 0, confirming no distortion of the density profile under standard hopping alone. For 0 < λ < 1/2, a double- peak structure emerges with maxima near t = τ/4 and t = 3τ/4, which collapses into a single peak near t = τ/2 for λ ≥1/2. No double-peak structure is observed for λ < 0.

FIG. 4. The von Neumann entropy S(t) as a function of time t and parameter λ for one Bloch period. At λ = 0, the entropy vanishes, confirming that standard hopping alone generates no inter-particle correlations. As |λ| increases, the density-assisted tunnelling builds up correlations between particles, with the entropy being higher for negative λ. The entropy returns to zero at t = τ reflecting the period- icity of the Bloch dynamics.

FIG. 5. Early-time entropy generation coefficient c2 as a function of λ and Gaussian width σ. Inset shows c2 plotted against T 2, collapsing onto a straight line. Bottom-right panel shows the initial-state site occupations ni0, ni0±1, and ni0±2 at the central, nearest-neighbour, and next-nearest-neighbour sites as a function of σ.
